newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM says Karachi violence hitting economy.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM says Karachi violence hitting economy.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday continuation of violence in the port city of Karachi would offset his government's reforms to revive the ailing economy.
"It is necessary to improve the law and order situation in Karachi, otherwise all the measures taken by the government to boost the economy would make no impact," he told reporters.

There has been a renewed surge in political violence in the troubled city, in which dozens have died in target killings and attacks during the past few weeks between the rival factions of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM).
Saturday's killing of the chief of the state-owned Karachi Electric Supply Corporation, Shahid Hamid, by gunmen drew protests from political parties.

Hamid's widow had lodged a complaint against the MQM, which is a coalition partner in the government of Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, with Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party.
"Anti-Pakistan forces are active all over the country," Sharif said. "We have proofs that funds are being pumped in from outside to destabilise Pakistan."
Police say more than 160 people have been killed in Karachi's political violence since March 1, compared to 500 in 1996 and more than 2,000 in 1995.
Earlier on Tuesday, ambulance workers picked up the body of a youngster from the volatile Korangi area stuffed in a gunny bag, while an 11-year-old boy was shot dead in overnight violence.
Sharif said a meeting he held on Tuesday with provincial authorities had reviewed law and order in Karachi and decided on steps to restore peace.
"We have to improve law and order at every cost," he said. "The police and (paramilitary) rangers have been put on alert." He did not elaborate.
Sharif said PML and MQM would jointly fight terrorism.
"The MQM also wants peace and will help to end violence in the city," he said.
The previous government of prime minister Benazir Bhutto had blamed the MQM for most of the violence in Karachi and launched a crackdown against the party.
The movement denied the charge and accused security forces of carrying out summary killings of its workers.
The MQM represents Urdu-speaking people who migrated from India at partition in 1947 and their descendants.
